name: Copper
short: Case reports: copper supplements (30-60 mg/day, 3 years) caused cirrhosis needing a transplant; 30 g copper sulfate poisoning: fatal. Trial, 60 apparently healthy men, 8 mg/day: liver tests unchanged.
text: A case report describes an adult in whom copper supplements taken at 30-60 mg a day for 3 years caused severe liver cirrhosis that required a liver transplant. Another case report describes a 32-year-old bodybuilder using many nutritional, performance-enhancing and weight-loss supplements who developed life-threatening encephalopathy, liver failure, muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) and copper toxicity mimicking Wilson's disease; the abstract does not name which product supplied the copper. Copper salts swallowed in poisoning amounts are a different situation from supplements: a young woman who swallowed 30 g of copper sulfate developed acute kidney injury, severe breakdown of red blood cells and methaemoglobinaemia by the second day and died 48 hours after arriving at hospital, and the authors describe rapid progression to liver and kidney failure. In contrast, in a 6-month randomised placebo-controlled trial in 60 apparently healthy men in Chile, 8 mg of copper a day (as copper sulfate) had no effect on liver enzymes (transaminases), serum copper or ceruloplasmin. A 2024 review states that even small changes in copper concentration may be associated with significant toxicity. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
